title: The House on the Rock and the House on the Sand
description: Jesus concludes the Sermon on the Mount with the parable of two builders: The wise man who heard Jesus' words and acted on them built his house on the rock, and it stood firm when the rain poured down, the rivers flooded, and the winds beat against it. The foolish man who heard the words but did not act on them built on sand, and the house collapsed with a great crash. The crowd was amazed at Jesus' teaching, for he spoke with authority, not like their teachers of the law.

versions.title: Houses on the Rock and on the Sand
versions.description: Jesus concludes the Sermon on the Mount with the parable of the wise man who built his house on the rock and the foolish man who built on sand. The parable emphasizes the importance of hearing and acting on Jesus' words.
versions.reason: [minor] references: Verses 28-29 are a conclusion to the Sermon on the Mount as a whole, not directly part of the parable. But they naturally belong as the closing of the speech.

versions.reason: [minor] references: Verses 28-29 are the conclusion to the entire Sermon on the Mount, not part of the parable itself. However, they thematically belong with the conclusion.; [major] overall: The narrative of the Sermon on the Mount already covers Matt 5:1–7:29, including this parable. Nevertheless, the parable of the house on the rock is a clearly defined teaching unit that can well stand as its own story under Jesus' parables.
